## a79fb4ad1f55

**Classification: reproduced validator/domain shortcut / missing noncrossing case.**  
Target generator SHA-256: `544a0f28ff4ee95eb2006c0b66d5b0b272fdedc8470bba6a8ca6229980964377`.  
Rule hash: `30803831667e`.

The target self-check verifies that color-2 markers share a row and color-3 markers share a column, but it does not require their finite endpoint spans to intersect. The default generator always places endpoints around an intersection. Consequently the shortcut **paint the intersection of the infinite supporting row and column** agrees with default scenes even when the intended finite-segment rule should produce no mark.

I constructed a 7×8 input with color-2 endpoints at `(2,1)` and `(2,3)`, and color-3 endpoints at `(0,6)` and `(4,6)`. The validator accepts it. The infinite-line rival paints cyan 8 at `(2,6)`, but column 6 lies outside the finite color-2 segment from columns 1 through 3, so the actual Racket output is all zeros.

A scan of seeds 0–19 and sample indices 0–9 at medium difficulty found **0/200** generated inputs whose supporting lines meet outside at least one finite endpoint span. The distribution therefore never refuted this shortcut in the scanned census despite the validator admitting such a case.

Exact input, outputs, hashes, validator result, scan denominator, and reproduction command: `checks/audit-a79fb4ad1f55-counterexample.json`.

## Audit reproduction

Both findings were generated in one Racket-backed read-only run from the packet root:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 ../checks/audit_probe_runner.py
```

Console confirmation: `checks/audit-probe-console.log`.
